I will keep things simple and steady this year. In Quzhou County, the crop pattern I know best and trust most is winter wheat followed by summer maize on the same land. At my age, I do not want to take big market or management risks with crops that need more labor, more skill, or more uncertain selling. Wheat and maize fit my local soil, local weather, local machines, and the water conditions I am used to managing. I will stay with improved winter wheat seed and hybrid summer maize seed because they are more stable for yield than old seed I keep myself. I will use fertilizer in a moderate way, not too little and not too much, because I want a reliable harvest and I do not want to waste money. For wheat, I will irrigate at the key stages and spray mainly when disease or insects are likely. After wheat harvest, I will move quickly into summer maize, keep tillage light to save labor and moisture, and manage water and pests closely during the hot season. My goal is not the highest possible yield. My goal is a steady yield, lower risk, and work I can finish on time.
